For p>2 the strict increase of elasticity E_p from 1 to >2 proves a unique interior maximum of H_p, giving precisely one global aspect cutoff, an explicit oblique maximizer before it, and six contacts at it. The quartic radical follows algebraically. A standalone standard-library verifier passed quadratures and exact-radical checks; finite tests are supporting not proofs. value.rationale: Euclidean radius extremization is not affine invariant even though radial mean bodies are. Nonsquare rectangles are the canonical one-parameter anisotropic deformation of the square, making their ordinary Euclidean extremizers a motivated open benchmark beyond known square and cube formulas. The result gives a full real-exponent and aspect-ratio classification, four ever-oblique inradius contacts, a discontinuous four/six/two circumradius contact transition, and an exact quartic algebraic threshold. These are structural geometric equality cases, not an arbitrary parameter substitution or mere recomputation of the known covariogram.
